status: Approved by John on 5 November 2026 in the Chicory spread
prompt:
Create one wide instructional illustration strip, with three distinct scenes evenly spaced left to right, on a genuinely transparent background. Use a landscape canvas approximately 3:1. No text, numbers, letters, arrows, labels, borders or panels anywhere. The attached image is STYLE REFERENCE ONLY: match the existing gardening book's clear coloured pencil/watercolour instructional drawing, realistic simplified proportions, warm tan roots and soil, green leaves, clean fine edges and restrained shading. Do not copy its subjects or layout.
Subject: the three stages of forcing Witloof chicory roots for pale winter chicons. All objects fully visible and separated by generous clear space. Scenes share the same baseline and overall height, approximately the same visual weight, and each remains within its own equal third of the canvas.
LEFT: a single freshly lifted substantial tapered buff-coloured chicory taproot, upright, with only short green cut leaf stubs above its broad crown, intact tiny centre growing point, and a few restrained lateral roots. A pair of small gardening scissors beside the top makes the trimming operation clear; the blades lie above the crown, never cutting the bud or root. No mature head and no long green leaves.
CENTRE: a deep terracotta flowerpot shown in educational cutaway. Three long tapered buff chicory roots stand vertically, side by side, their root tips inside the pot and buried in dark moist compost. Crowns and short cut leaf stubs remain clearly exposed just above the compost surface, slightly below pot rim. Show a cutaway through the front wall and soil so the three buried roots and correct depth are unmistakable. Do not show free-floating roots or roots sticking through the bottom.
RIGHT: the same terracotta pot seen normally from outside, with three short pale cream-yellow tightly packed chicory chicons emerging. An inverted opaque dark charcoal plastic bucket is held slightly above this pot by a cropped hand entering from upper right, ready to lower over it. The bucket has a broad open mouth pointing DOWN, a flat closed bottom on top, and is clearly wide enough to fit over the pot rim and tall enough to enclose the shoots with headroom. The bucket is solid black/charcoal, not transparent, not a glass cloche and not a dome. Its small gap above the pot is only to demonstrate the removable cover. No soil or roots float outside the pot. Quiet natural colours, readable at small book size. Use the whole strip with modest transparent outer margins.
iconMethod: Editable SVG matching the coloured icon vocabulary; opaque upturned bucket over forcing pot, not a cloche.
visualCheck: Trimmed leaf stubs retain central growing point; cutaway shows roots buried with crowns exposed; opaque inverted bucket can cover pale shoots. No generated labels. The new strip intentionally replaces the two generic sow/thin drawings in this proposal; their original files and baseline proof remain intact.
